expected_probes.reasoning: Lowercase drive letter: ntpath.normpath preserves the drive case (no folding); the component-wise resolver yields '/c:/repo/AGENTS.md'. Windows drive letters are case-insensitive, so 'c:' and 'C:' name the same drive but different canonical strings (finding F5).
Drive root: ntpath.normpath('C:\') is 'C:\' -> 'C:/'. Resolution drops the trailing separator ('/C:' -- one component, '/C:' does not exist on Linux, so the rest is appended lexically).

UNC with '..': backslashes become '/', '..' resolves lexically without popping above the share ('//server/share' is the floor). Resolved is the canonical minus one leading slash (S0 fs/windows precedent).
Bare UNC root: '\\server\share' -> '//server/share'; resolved '/server/share'. No trailing component to resolve.
Unicode drive path: separators normalise, unicode passes through byte-for-byte (Q3, no NFC/NFD normalisation). Resolved is '/'+canonical.

Drive-relative spelling through canonicalize: is_windows_style_path requires a separator after the colon, so 'C:foo\bar' is NOT detected as Windows-style and is joined onto cwd as a relative path (backslash is a filename character on Linux). The drive-relative rejection in normalize_windows_path is NOT reached from canonicalize (finding F4, same mechanism as win-drive-relative-import). {corpus} is the fixtures/windows directory.
Mixed separators: backslashes become '/', forward slashes stay; duplicate separators collapse. Resolved is '/'+canonical.
Single-dot component resolves lexically ('.' drops out). Resolved is '/'+canonical.

'..' never pops above the drive root: 'C:\repo\..\..\outside' clamps to 'C:\outside' (ntpath semantics; the Oracle's normpath_posix clamps absolute '..' at the root the same way). Resolved is '/'+canonical.
Trailing separator is removed (except for the filesystem root). Resolved is '/'+canonical.
